citation: Bedford L, Hay D, Devoy A, Paine S, Powe DG, Seth R, et al. Depletion of 26S proteasomes in mouse brain neurons causes neurodegeneration and Lewy-like inclusions resembling human pale bodies. The Journal of Neuroscience. 2008. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.2218-08.2008.
description: Conditional Psmc1/Rpt2 deletion in mouse substantia nigra or forebrain neurons depleted 26S proteasomes while sparing 20S proteasomes and caused ubiquitin-positive intraneuronal inclusions and extensive neurodegeneration. This is direct target-specific evidence that Psmc1 loss disrupts neuronal proteasome homeostasis.

citation: Radhakrishnan SK, den Besten W, Deshaies RJ. p97-dependent retrotranslocation and proteolytic processing govern formation of active Nrf1 upon proteasome inhibition. eLife. 2014. doi:10.7554/eLife.01856.
description: This study documents the conserved mammalian bounce-back response in which proteasome inhibition stabilizes and processes Nrf1/NFE2L1, enabling activation of proteasome subunit mRNAs. It supplies the mechanistic link from proteasome impairment to compensatory proteasome-gene induction.

citation: Tomlin FM, Gerling-Driessen UIM, Liu YC, Flynn RA, Vangala JR, Lentz CS, et al. Inhibition of NGLY1 inactivates the transcription factor Nrf1 and potentiates proteasome inhibitor cytotoxicity. ACS Central Science. 2017. doi:10.1021/acscentsci.7b00224.
description: The paper shows that NGLY1 is required for Nrf1 activation and for the proteasome-subunit gene expression induced by proteasome insufficiency or pharmacologic inhibition. It independently supports the expected direction of proteasome bounce-back after impaired 26S proteasome function.

citation: Yu ZQ, Carmichael J, Collins GA, D'Agostino MD, Lessard M, Firth HV, et al. PSMC5 insufficiency and P320R mutation impair proteasome function. Human Molecular Genetics. 2024. doi:10.1093/hmg/ddae085.
description: PSMC5 loss-of-function and the P320R neurodevelopmental-disorder variant impaired proteasome activity, with P320R weakening 19S regulatory-particle association with the 20S core and PSMC5 insufficiency activating apoptosis in cells. This gives target-specific evidence that reducing PSMC5 disrupts the 26S proteasome.

citation: Kury S, Stanton JE, van Woerden GM, Bosc-Rosati A, Hsieh TC, Bray L, et al. Investigating the neuronal role of the proteasomal ATPase subunit gene PSMC5 in neurodevelopmental proteasomopathies. Nature Communications. 2025. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-65556-8.
description: The study identifies pathogenic PSMC5/RPT6 variants and reports that loss of PSMC5/RPT6 impairs proteasome activity, promotes protein aggregation, perturbs mitochondrial homeostasis, lipid metabolism and immune signaling, and compromises synaptic balance and neuritogenesis. It is target-specific neuronal support for interpreting Psmc5 perturbation as proteasome dysfunction.

citation: Wu W, Ahmad K, Henikoff S. Chromatin-bound U2AF2 splicing factor ensures exon inclusion. Molecular Cell. 2025. doi:10.1016/j.molcel.2025.04.013.
description: CUT&RUN and knockdown experiments in K562 cells showed that U2AF2 binds intron-containing genes, has greater occupancy at exons skipped after U2AF2 knockdown, and targets genes encoding splicing factors to improve splicing accuracy and efficiency. This supports a specific U2AF2-to-splicing-factor-homeostasis bridge without defining the mRNA direction observed in mouse neurons.

citation: Tari M, Manceau V, de Matha Salone J, Kobayashi A, Pastre D, Maucuer A. U2AF65 assemblies drive sequence-specific splice site recognition. EMBO Reports. 2019. doi:10.15252/embr.201847604.
description: The paper shows that U2AF65 interacts with SF3B155 and that U2AF65 knockdown changes inclusion of cassette exons preceded by repeated pyrimidine-rich motifs. It supports the expected class of U2AF2-dependent splice-site effects but not transcript-level direction for Rsrp1, Srrm2, or Luc7l2.

citation: Li Y, Wang X, Qi S, Gao L, Huang G, Ren Z, et al. Spliceosome-regulated RSRP1-dependent NF-kappaB activation promotes the glioblastoma mesenchymal phenotype. Neuro-Oncology. 2021. doi:10.1093/neuonc/noab126.
description: Transcriptomic and functional analyses showed that RSRP1 regulates alternative splicing by mediating spliceosome assembly. This establishes RSRP1 as a spliceosome-associated response gene but does not directly connect U2AF2 loss to RSRP1 mRNA down-regulation.
